title: Blanch and Shock
description: A seconds-long boil followed by an ice bath — how green things stay GREEN.

steps.text: Drop the greens into rapidly boiling water — 10 seconds for tender herbs, up to a minute for sturdy vegetables.
steps.why: The brief heat kills the enzymes that turn greens brown and muddy over time.
The shock stops the cooking at exactly the moment you chose and locks the chlorophyll at its brightest.

steps.text: Squeeze or pat completely dry before using.
steps.why: Clinging water dilutes whatever the greens go into next — a basil oil goes cloudy, a sauté spits.
